PLEASE TAKE NOTICE, that the defendants, ANTHONY F. FERRARA and METRO-
NORTH COMMUTER RAILROAD, by their attorneys MILBER MAKRIS PLOUSADIS & 
SEIDEN, LLP as and for their Bill of Particulars, allege as follows: 
MVA-CULPABLE CONDUCT/ASSUMPTION OF THE RISK 
The plaintiff was reckless, careless and negligent in the ownership, operation, 
maintenance, management, control, repair, supervision and inspection of her motor vehicle in 
that the plaintiff failed to observe the conditions on the roadway and have a due, timely, adequate 
and proper lookout for traffic along the aforesaid roadway, in failing to give any warning, notice 
or signal with regard to maneuvering her vehicle, in operating her vehicle at an excessive rate of 
speed in that plaintiff failed to exercise reasonable, due care and caution in failing to make 
adequate, proper and timely use of the brakes and failing to have said motor vehicle under 
reasonable and proper control, in failing to keep said vehicle at a reasonable and sufficient 
distance away from other vehicles so as to avoid sudden and unexpected maneuvers, stops and 
starts, in failing to use directional signals, in failing to utilize the horn, in failing to keep a proper 
lookout for traffic along the roadway, in failing what was there to be seen, in failing to use 
proper means and precautions to avoid, warn and guard against the happening of the accident, in

failing to observe the rules of the road and thereby causing and contributing to the contact 
between the vehicles.  
SEAT BELT 
Plaintiffs were careless and negligent in failing to utilize an available seat belt and 
plaintiff’s failure to use the available seat belt caused, exacerbated, and contributed to their 
alleged damages herein.   
SERIOUS INJURY 
This request is objected as being palpably improper.  The burden of proof is upon the 
plaintiff to prove a serious injury pursuant to the Insurance Law of the State of New York. 
FAILURE TO MITIGATE DAMAGES-PERSONAL INJURY 
Plaintiff failed to mitigate her damages by refusing proper medical care at the time and 
place of the occurrence, by failing to seek timely and appropriate medical care, by failing to 
properly adhere to the instructions of her medical providers, by disregarding medical advices, by 
refusing appropriate treatment, by failing to comply with medical instructions, by failing to seek 
appropriate medical care, and by otherwise failing to take appropriate steps to ensure that she 
properly recovered from the injuries she sustained. 
COLLATERAL SOURCE- PERSONAL INJURY 
Upon information and belief, any past or future costs or expenses incurred or to be 
incurred by the plaintiff for medical care, dental care, custodial care or rehabilitative services, 
loss of earnings or other economic loss, has been or will with reasonable certainty be replaced or 
indemnified in whole or in part from a collateral source as defined in Section 4545(c) of the Civil 
Practice Law and Rules and, therefore, any judgment awarded to the plaintiff in this action shall 
be reduced by the amount of any past or future cost or expense which has or will be replaced or 
indemnified in whole or in part from said collateral source.

EMERGENCY DOCTRINE 
At all times, defendant acted reasonably due to a sudden condition/event which could not 
have been reasonably anticipated and which such sudden condition/event defendant did not cause 
or contribute to. 
                PLEASE TAKE FURTHER NOTICE, that the defendant presently lacks sufficient 
knowledge to respond further to those items demanded.  When the requisite knowledge to 
respond is acquired a further response will be provided.  See Major v. General Motors 
Corp.,  126 A.D.2d 521, 510 N.Y.S.2d 643 (2d Dept. 1987).
